summary: The root حذر (Hdhr) conveys caution, wariness, and vigilance. It describes someone who is prepared, on guard, or fearful.
lane: حَذِرٌ ذ (S, A, Msb, K) and (S, A, K) Cautious; wary; vigilant; on his guard; careful; (S;) or in a state of preparation; (Msb;) as also ; (S, A, Msb;) and fearful: (S:) or very cautious or wary or vigilant or careful; as also (K) and : (A, K:) or this last signifies very fearful and cautious &c.: (S:) pl. of the first حَذِرُونَ and حَذَارَى . (S, K.) Sb cites, as an ex. of حَذِرٌ used transitively, حَذِرٌ أُمُورًا لَا تُخَافُ وَ آمِنٌ مَا لَيْسَ مُنْجِيهِ مِنَ الأَقْدَارِ [ Cautious, or very cautious, of things not to be feared, and trusting in that which will not save him from the decrees of destiny ]: but this is extr.; for an epithet of the measure فَعِلٌ is not [regularly] trans., so as to govern an objective complement. (S, TA.) In the Kur xxvi. 56, some read ; and some, حَذِرُونَ and : حاذرون signifying in a state of preparation; (Zj, S;) or fully equipped with arms: (Sh:) and حذرون , in a state of fear; (S;) or in a state of preparation; (TA;) or in a state of preparation with the accoutrements of war; (Ibn-Mes'ood;) or cautious, or vigilant. (Zj.)

headwords.def: aor. حَ َرَ, inf. n. حَ َرٌ; and; (Msb, K;) He was cautious, wary, or vigilant; was on his guard; took care; (K, TA;) was in a state of preparation; (Msb;) was in fear; feared. (TA.) [You say, حَ ِرَ مِنْ أَمْرٍ and مِنْهُ He was cautious, &c., of a thing, or an event. And حَ ِرَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كَ َا and He was cautious, &c., for him, of such a thing. And both verbs are also trans.: for you say,] حَ ِرَهُ, (S, A, Msb,) aor. and inf. n.

[The cautioning another; putting him on his guard; making him to be cautious or wary or vigilant, to be on his guard, to take care, or to be in a state of preparation; ] the making to fear, or be in fear. (S, TA.) [You say, ح ّرهُ مِنْ أَمْرٍ He cautioned him against a thing. And the verb is also doubly trans.: you say,] ح ّرهُ الأَمْرَ [ He cautioned him against, or made him to fear, the thing, or event ]. (TA.) And أَحَ ِّرُكَهُ [ I caution thee against him, or it ].

(TK,) inf. n. مُحَا َرَةٌ (S, K) and حِ َارٌ, (S,) They two were cautious, or in fear, each of the other; were on their guard, or in a state of preparation, each against the other. (TK.) حِ َارٌ is syn. with مُحَا َرَةٌ, (S,) and مُحَا َرَةٌ is between two. (K.) See also 1, in two places.
إِحْتَ َرَ see 1, in five places.

احدارّ احدار He was angry, (K,) and prepared himself to do mischief, (TA,) and drew himself together ( تَقَبَّضَ ): so in some copies of the K and in other lexicons: or became enraged ( تَغَيَّظَ ): so in other copies of the K. (TA.)
: see what next follows, in two places.

and, (S, A, Msb, K,) the former an inf. n., (S, Msb,) and the latter a simple subst., (Msb,) Caution, wariness, vigilance, guard, or care; (S, A, K;) as also; (K;) or a state of preparation; (Msb;) or fear; (Mgh, * TA;) and so: (S, Msb, K:) [pl. أَحْ َارٌ.] You say, أَخَ َ He took care; was cautious, or vigilant. (Bd in iv. 73 and 103.) And هُوَ ٱبْنُ أَحْ َارٍ (tropical:) He is a son [i. e. a person ] of resolution, or determination, and caution, or wariness.
and its pl.: see what next follows.

(S, A, Msb, K) and (S, A, K) Cautious; wary; vigilant; on his guard; careful; (S;) or in a state of preparation; (Msb;) as also; (S, A, Msb;) and fearful: (S:) or very cautious or wary or vigilant or careful; as also (K) and: (A, K:) or this last signifies very fearful and cautious &c.: (S:) pl. of the first حَ ِرُونَ and حَ َارَى. (S, K.) Sb cites, as an ex.

A rugged piece of ground: (S, K:) or the top of a mountain, when it is hard and rugged, but level: (Aboo-Kheyreh:) and rough ground: (TA:) and a rugged [ hill such as is termed ] أَكَمَة; as also: (K:) pl. حَ َارَى and حَ َارٍ. (S.) Also The عِفْرِيَة [or feathers of the back of the neck ] of a cock: (S, K:) pl. as above. (K)
: see what next precedes.
: see حَ ِرٌ.
[like البُ ُرَّى,] What is false, vain, or ineffectual; syn. البَاطِلُ. (K.)

[an imperative verbal noun] meaning Beware; be cautious, wary, or on thy guard; or take care. (S, A, K.) The poet (Abu-n-Nejm, TA) says, حَ َارِ مِنْ أَرْمَاحِنَا حَ َارِ Beware of our spears: beware. (S, A.) And you say, سُمِعَتْ حَ َارِ فِى عَسْكَرِهِمْ [The cry “ Beware ” was heard in their army ].

[ A cautioner ]. You say, أَنَا حَ ِيرُكَ مِنْهُ i. e. مُحَ ِّرُكَ [ I am thy cautioner against him, or it ]; (TA;) or أُحَ ِّرُكَهُ [ I caution thee against him, or it ]: (K:) known to As as heard only from Lth. (TA.) [See also what next follows.]
Persons who make others to fear: (K:) or rather, as others than F explain it, مُنْ ِرُونَ [ cautioners, or warners, &c.]. (TA.)
and حَا ِرُونَ: see حَ ِرٌ.
: see حَ ِرٌ.
[ More, and most, cautious, wary, vigilant, careful, or fearful ]. You say, أَحْ َرُ مِنَ الغُرَابِ More fearful [or cautious, &c.] than the raven: a prov. (Mgh.)
A thing that is feared. (Msb.) One says, وَقَاكَ ٱللّٰهُ كُلَّ مَحْ ُورٍ [ May God preserve thee from everything that is feared ]. (A.)

A calamity that is feared, or regarded with caution: (K:) or a troop of horse making a hostile attack, or incursion, upon a people: or i. q. صَيْحَةٌ [app. as meaning a hostile attack, or incursion, when it comes upon a tribe suddenly, or unexpectedly; or it may here mean a punishment, or chastisement; or a crying-out, which is the primary signification]: (A:) and war. (K.) See also حَ َرٌ, in two places.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
